correctness.rationale: The checker enumerates every possible vertex subset of the ten-vertex Petersen graph and constructs all ordinary k-cut faces for k=5,6,7. The three explicit element matchings are confirmed acyclic by whole-Hasse-graph topological sorting. Their Morse chain modules yield one critical vertex and respectively five 3-cells plus nine 4-cells, eleven 3-cells, and eleven 1-cells. For the mixed-dimensional case, the exact signed 5x9 Morse boundary has a 4x4 unit minor and fifth row linearly dependent on the first four, giving four Smith units and reducing the attaching maps (which live in pi_3 of a wedge of 3-spheres) to four trivializable pairs. Thus the full integral homotopy equivalences follow; separate GF(2) chain ranks agree. No infinity assertion is made.

originality.rationale: The 2023 defining paper, checked in its article text, treats the Petersen graph as a k=2 instance, not its k=5,6,7 terminal ordinary cut complexes. Previously reported lower-parameter fourth-cut results do not determine these terminal levels. Several independent published-finding corpus searches found same-graph statements only for smaller k or for different complexes, and the broader high-girth cut-complex theorem has an unsatisfied girth hypothesis. Searches of primary paper titles and publicly indexed material did not reveal an implication or exact table with the stated mixed-dimensional k=5 classification. Residual risk is explicitly recorded; this is best-evidence originality rather than mathematical proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: No finite search proves worldwide novelty; unindexed or offline computations may duplicate the terminal profile.

value.rationale: This is the complete nonvoid terminal ordinary cut-complex profile of the canonical 10-vertex Petersen graph, extending attention beyond its known smaller-parameter cut complexes. The k=5 complex is pure 4-dimensional yet has essential 3-dimensional integral homology, giving an explicit non-shellability obstruction and a sharp transition before the simple wedges at k=6,7. These are motivated complete topological invariants, not an arbitrary slice or a recomputed known table. A full integer attaching-map calculation, not just Euler characteristic or mod-two ranks, is necessary.
